Subject: Pilot credit request — multiple teams

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the note yesterday — Orchid is excited to be running the pilot. Our engineering and research teams have separately started evaluation workloads and we've hit the initial credit allotment faster than expected.

TL;DR: Can you grant an extra 100k tokens and extend the pilot for two weeks so both teams can finish the proof-of-concept? We can provide a short one-page scope and a PO if that helps.

We have three named users (sam.thompson, elena.vargas, finance@orchid.ai) but some of the test jobs are coming from targeted service accounts; happy to share identifiers. Attaching the pilot scope and a quick usage snapshot.

Attachments: pilot_scope.pdf (PDF)

Thanks — Elena
Elena Vargas
Head of Product
Orchid Labs

Quick triage notes (summary):

- Pattern: ~6 rapid token bursts from ORCH-77 across 3 service accounts, all within 48 hours. IPs resolve to a small set of cloud provider ranges but some motion indicates ephemeral Docker runners.
- History: ORCH-77 opened two pilot orgs in the last 45 days (one closed, new org opened).
- Risk level: medium-high for promo-chaining. Evidence attached + flagged Drive doc with sample traces.

Recommendation: place a temporary hold on granting extra promo credits, request verification from Orchid (PO + single point of contact confirmation + service account list), and require that tokens already consumed be reviewed before any extension. If verified and we can map teams to single consistent owners, consider a one-time top-up for a single service account rather than an org-wide extension.

Link: https://drive.redwood/reviews/ORCH-2028-pilot-evidence
Attachments: promo_request_form.docx

Ben Carter

Thanks team — tying policy + Ops here. Decision: we will not issue an org-wide extension at this time.

Action plan for resolution (final):
1) Jonas to request and confirm a PO and a named POC for the pilot from Orchid (we need contractual traceability).
2) Orchid provides the explicit list of service account IDs and the expected test schedule; Redwood fraud ops will validate activity against that list.
3) If verification demonstrates single-owner, low-risk usage for one service account, Redwood will grant a one-time 50k token extension scoped to that service account only and extend the pilot two weeks.
4) If evidence of account reopenings / coordinated reuse remains, deny extension and apply a promo-block to the offending service accounts.

Jonas — please relay the decision and the required docs to Orchid and mark the ticket SEC-4129 as awaiting customer evidence.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Policy
Redwood Inference
